.Breezy to locally windy conditions are bringing critical fire
weather conditions through the Grande Ronde Valley. Winds
expected to remain strong through the evening with RH values
dropping down as low as 23 percent.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 694 Grande Ronde Valley of
Oregon.

* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT this evening.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 23 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 9:21PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage on Saturday, but strong northeasterly winds will lead to a
faster rise by Saturday night. The river is forecast to reach
Moderate Flood Stage Sunday, with a steady increase through Moderate
Flood Stage forecast next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 2.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Friday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early
Tuesday afternoon. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Brewster, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 8:16PM CDT until October 18 at 10:12AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP, Texas affecting Brewster
County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande above Rio Conchos near
Presidio,  Texas, Test Forecast Point A, Rio Grande at Presidio
Vehicle Bridge, Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near
Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Dryden,  Texas, Terlingua Creek near Terlingua,
Texas...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP,
Texas.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, and no damage
is expected.  Preparations may be necessary to remove water pumps.
The park should be notified at this time if additional rises are
expected so they will have time to remove the pumps. At 13.0 feet,
the river reaches minor flood stage.  Water reaches the water pumps
maintained by the park service that are used to water the
campgrounds and to provide water to the employee living quarters.
It may be necessary for park personnel to remove the pumps. At 15.0
feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage.  Water pumps
submerge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 PM CDT Friday the stage was 10.8 feet (3.3 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 13.1 feet (4.0 meters) late this
evening. It will then fall below flood stage late this evening.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet (4.0 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 13.1
feet (4.0 meters) on 09/03/2022.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 830 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 8:13PM CDT until October 19 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande At Foster Ranch affecting Val Verde County.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Pecos River Near Langtry affecting Val Verde County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Foster Ranch.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, Lowland flooding makes low water crossings
at Pandale on the Pecos River and tributaries flooded and
impassable. At 7.0 feet, (2.1 meters), Minor lowland flooding is a
significant threat to swimmers, tubers and campers on the low banks
of the Pecos River above Pandale to above Langtry. At 10.0 feet,
(3.0 meters), Moderate flooding is well into the flood plain making
secondary roads and crossings along the Pecos River and tributaries
very dangerous to travel. Swimmers and tubers should leave the
river as flow is dangerously turbulent. Campers vehicles and gear
in the flood plain can be swept downstream.


* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 8.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage late tonight to
16.8 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It will then fall below flood
stage late tomorrow evening to 13.3 feet early Sunday morning. It
will rise to flood stage Sunday morning. It will then fall again
Sunday night.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 17 at 11:12AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT....Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more
are expected.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning Saturday night. Onset of
destructive winds Sunday morning. Damaging winds will continue into
at least Sunday night, possibly longer if conditions warrant.

* IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that
could damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically
reducing visibilities in heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly
toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to
change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal
waters, with damaging winds moving in late tonight and lasting
into at least Sunday night. Champi is expected to strengthen
further today as it approaches, then move through the region as a
typhoon Sunday morning. Seas will quickly rise, with significant
sea heights reaching as high as 35 feet during closest passage of
Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may continue into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for the passage of a
typhoon Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions are expected
to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely dangerous for any
vessels of larger size. As Tropical Storm Champi approaches, stay in
safe harbor.
